decision: Neither candidate adopted: successor retains GSO overload collapse; ACK resume improves GSO but regresses bridge throughput.

conditions.build: release, all features, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl; opt-level=3, lto=true, strip=true, codegen-units=1
conditions.isolation: All variants in one disposable no-NIC container image. No local builds, tests or Git packing during load. Separate-host kernel correctness tests ran concurrently.
conditions.windows: Goodput uses receiver snapshots; CPU/context switches use before/sent snapshots; protocol and drop counters use before/after, including drain. Missing fraction is final unique received / sent and includes drain.
conditions.cpu: 100% is one logical CPU. Per-CPU /proc/stat includes kernel and other host work and does not attribute that work exclusively to the daemon.
conditions.counter_units: Queue, ACK record, source SKB and frame drops differ; do not sum them into inner loss.
limitations: One sweep per candidate; controls bracket the pair, not each candidate separately.
Bridge offered load was generator-limited below the requested 5 Gbit/s.
No new candidate loss-injection, TCP or real-access throughput run.
No Linux 6.8 full runtime suite for these rejected candidates; library kernel suite passed there.
